title: Case: Recipient has been given two different delivery days for a two-person delivery
context: An oak wardrobe on a two-person delivery was rebooked at the recipient's request. Someone must be home to receive it and the recipient can take only one day off work.
initial_request: Sorry to chase. I need to tell my manager tonight which day I'm off, I can only do one of them not both, and somebody has to be in for the two man delivery. Is it Wednesday morning or Thursday afternoon? Just tell me which one and I'll book it.

events.body: DL-6072 (TG-8165, two-person delivery, oak wardrobe) rebooked at recipient request. Confirmed slot: Thursday 2026-04-16, 12:00–16:00 UTC. Booking ref SB-7432.
got a text from plover arc saying delivery WEDNESDAY 15th 8-12. the email from you lot says thursday. which
DL-6072: what date and window is on the route plan?

922 is on the two-man van for Wed 15/04, 08:00-12:00, went onto the plan Monday. Don't see a Thurs entry for it. We run what's on the plan. Bookings are Larkspire's, if their record says different they need to fix one or the other.

Sorry to chase. I need to tell my manager tonight which day I'm off, I can only do one of them not both, and somebody has to be in for the two man delivery. Is it Wednesday morning or Thursday afternoon? Just tell me which one and I'll book it.

DL-6072 (TG-8165, two-person delivery) has two different dates on record. Your confirmation this morning gives Thursday 2026-04-16, 12:00–16:00 UTC, booking ref SB-7432. Dispatch report it on the two-person van plan for Wednesday 2026-04-15, 08:00–12:00, loaded on Monday, with no Thursday entry, and the recipient has received a text giving the Wednesday slot. Please confirm which single slot is valid and have the other record corrected. The recipient, Kestra Corrigan, can take only one day off work and has to tell his employer this evening; the Wednesday window opens at 08:00 tomorrow. I have not told him either date.
FYI only, no action needed from the desk: we have this in hand and will update the customer directly. Nothing further is required from you on this one.

must_not: Sends another message to Larkspire, Gorsewick Arc Logistics restating the request already sent
Sends the customer a new promise, date or outcome that nobody has confirmed
Tells the recipient the delivery is on Wednesday, or that it is on Thursday
Asks Dispatch to move DL-6072 on the route plan
Advises the recipient to keep both days free or to take a day off on the strength of either record
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)

rationale: Rule-made from gen-103: people, organisations and references renamed. The desk's correct action was already sent (event 6) and the last message is an acknowledgement or FYI with no request, so nothing is owed. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's.
